<context query="human-oversight gate wrapping each tool executor" template="default" budget="8000">
<section name="Conventions" source="repo" priority="1">
<document source="docs/human-oversight.md" type="doc" relevance="0.99" tokens="463">
## Where it is enforced

1. **Definition time.** `apps/api/src/tools/defineTmsTool.ts:60-66`, `enforceIdempotent`,
   throws when a TMS tool is defined with `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` or `DELETE`. It covers
   only tools built through that factory.
2. **Call time.** `apps/api/src/oversight/oversightHooks.ts:29`, the
   `requires_human_action` branch of the `oversight` fragment on HAL Engine's
   `beforeToolCall` hook, returns the declined result, and the engine then never calls
   the executor. The hook fires before every call to a registered tool, whichever file
   registered it. `supportAgentHooks` in `apps/api/src/server.ts` installs the fragment
   first in the one `composeHooks([...])` array, as a `firstOrFail` chain: a fragment
   can decline or abstain, never allow, and if the policy itself throws, the engine
   declines the call instead of running it.

Two backstops keep the table honest. `assertAllToolsDeclared`, called from
`apps/api/src/server.ts` before the port opens, refuses to start the api while a
registered tool has no row, and names the tool. A test fails when any table row other
than the fixture is not `read_only`, so the first write tool cannot merge before
approve-then-execute (#47) lands.

Until `@re-cinq/hal-engine` 0.3.0 the gate wrapped each executor at registration,
because no hook fired around a tool call. Since 0.3.0 it runs on `beforeToolCall`
(#193); the table and the declined result carried over unchanged, and the wrapper is
gone. `apps/api/src/tools/registerTools.ts` stays the only file under `apps/api/src/`
that may call `.register(`, and a CI step fails any other. The one wrapper it still
applies is the crash guard (#185), which declines nothing: it turns an executor's throw
into one `tool_crash` audit row and one `tool_crashed` escalation. It has no
customer-scope resolver yet; #18 adds it.
</document>
<document source="specs/support-agent-human-oversight/spec.md" type="spec" relevance="0.95" tokens="355">
## Issue Map

| Issue | Title                                                                     | Contributes                                                                                                 | State                               |
| ----- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------- |
| #33   | Enforce human oversight over every consequential tool call                | `ToolAuthority`, authority table, deny by default, startup check, blocked result, `docs/human-oversight.md` | Open                                |
| #47   | Perform a consequential action only after a named OLT human authorises it | Approve-then-execute: action catalogue, `request_authorised_action`, executor, write key, `records_intent`  | Blocked: KU-20 (conditional), KU-02 |
| #50   | Compose the support agent's orchestrator hook fragments into one object   | `composeHooks`, `thread` and `all` chains, exhaustive `HOOK_KINDS`, single-registration grep                | Open                                |
| #193  | Run the oversight gate on the engine's beforeToolCall hook, fail closed   | `firstOrFail` chain, `oversightHooks.ts`, removal of the per-executor wrapper                               | Open                                |
</document>
</section>

**session-summary/2026-09-12-repair-build-ci-verdict** (memory): Diagnosed assembly run 997026f5 (implementation-loop, issue #1510, PR #1684) and shipped PR #2039.

FINDING: the run did not die running tests. Four rounds came back red on ONE job (format) for ONE eslint error (specs/testing-standards/spec.md:7 require-status-matches-coverage). await-ci returned `failed` (ci_red_unchanged) → repair-build. ciFeedbackOf (apps/floor/src/work/assembly-run/ci-feedback.ts) rendered the "CI reported failures" block only for incoming outcome changes_requested; the await-ci→repair-build edge fires on failed. So repair-build — the node the YAML says "is handed the failing checks" — got NO verdict, ran `npm ci` + `npm run build -w @re-cinq/lore-shared`, and died at the 1Gi pod limit (BackoffLimitExceeded) on a one-line fix. ci_failure_summary was "" because Actions check-run output is null; #2021 (09-11, after the run) added steps+tail; the annotations endpoint had the exact path:line message and nothing read it.

SHIPPED (#2039, 4 commits): gate widened to failed+changes_requested; JobFailure.annotations (failure level, paginated) rendered first; explainFailedChecks moved from stations park-readers to shared check-runs.ts; new port reads listBranchCommits(repo, branch, limit) oldest-first + jobLog; lore-api GET /api/repos/:o/:r/ci-failures?branch|pr_number and /ci-jobs/:job_id/log?tail&grep; MCP tools lore_get_ci_failures / lore_get_ci_job_log in ci-tools.ts registered in registerSharedTools (agent gateway serves them), lore_get_pr_status moved beside them; detectCurrentBranch() in server-core repo-detect (uncached, null on detached HEAD). fix-ci prompt: act on annotation with an editor, ask CI via the tools, never reinstall/rebuild. NO migration: fix-ci org row is NULL since 0068 and resolves from the yaml in the image. OpenAPI + web-ui types + catalog seed regenerated; specs for both routes and both tools; FR15, shared-utilities, platform-infrastructure amended.

DECISIONS: user first got my "keep reads Floor-side, no pod tools" recommendation, reaffirmed pod tools → treated as their call; then asked for branch-keyed inputs (a pod never reliably knows a PR number) → routes accept branch or pr_number, tool defaults branch from git.

TRAPS: max-lines (300) hit on platform-github.ts (two-port adapter) → file-level eslint-disable with justification. Link re-anchoring needed a HEAD-line+title script handling empty labels, backticked labels, repo-root paths, untracked spec files, duplicate titles; run prettier BEFORE relink. memory-tools/pipeline-tools mcp tests fail locally pre-existing (clean HOME too) — judge by CI.
</document>
<document source="dod/halengine-issue-95-onerror-non-error-rejection" type="memory" tokens="993">
**dod/halengine-issue-95-onerror-non-error-rejection** (memory): DoD for HAL Engine (@re-cinq/hal-engine, GitHub repo re-cinq/HALEngine) issue #95 "Call onError for a rejection that is not an Error" (branch lore/implementation-loop/issue-95) -> success, strategy `direct`. Pushed bfb030c; origin/main had no drift (Already up to date).

CENTRAL CLAIM: src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.ts catch (L126-130) gates onError on `error instanceof Error`, so a non-Error rejection (string, plain object, undefined) bypasses onError while still propagating to the caller. Sibling of #94 (beforeSession escaping try) — both were the two remaining "Measured semantics — out of scope" flaw bullets in specs/hal-engine-config-hooks/spec.md.

RED TEST (one, in src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts inside describe('onError')): 'wraps a non-Error rejection in an Error whose cause is the original and still rejects the caller with the original'. Loops 3 cases (string/object/undefined) via new helper createRejectingProvider(value:unknown) that throws value; new helper rejectionOf(promise) returns the caller's raw rejection by identity (outcomeOf only returns .message, useless for a string/undefined rejection). Asserts per case {onErrorCallCount:1, isError:true, causeIsOriginal: passed instanceof Error && passed.cause===value, callerReceivedOriginal: rejection===value}. Fails today: count 0, isError false, causeIsOriginal false; callerReceivedOriginal already true both before/after (propagation unchanged) — so the red is exactly onError being skipped. NOTE the undefined case can't distinguish set-cause from unset (cause===undefined either way); its red comes from onErrorCallCount only, which is the honest signal. Ran: `NODE_OPTIONS=--experimental-vm-modules node node_modules/jest/bin/jest.js src/orchestration/chatOrchestrator.test.ts` -> 1 failed, 23 passed.

IMPLEMENTER OWES (facets in .lore/dod.md): in the catch, wrap a non-Error in new Error(...) with {cause:error}, leave an Error as-is, call onError; keep `throw error` re-throwing the ORIGINAL value unchanged. Criterion 3 (Error reaches onError as same instance) is pinned by existing onError tests staying unedited — NO new test owed. CHANGELOG [Unreleased] entry (implementer): hook typed against Error now fires for rejections it never saw; caller boundary value unchanged.

SPEC: added guarantee bullet in "Installing hooks through config" citing the test; REMOVED the instanceof-Error flaw bullet from "Measured semantics — out of scope" and changed intro "three properties"->"two properties" (matches what #94 did to the beforeSession bullet; if both merge there WILL be a conflict on that intro line + the two removed bullets — resolve by keeping both removals and "one/zero properties").

ENV/TOOLING (confirmed still true 2026-09-25): pod arrived with NO node_modules; `npm ci` (exit 0) needed first. ts-jest ESM jest30; run one file with `node node_modules/jest/bin/jest.js <path>` + NODE_OPTIONS=--experimental-vm-modules (path present -> guard scoped-allow). Guard hook refuses any bash line where jest/test/vitest appears as a bare word after &&/;/| — even `echo`/`[ -e .../jest ]` trips it; keep a file path in the runner invocation. Formatter `npx prettier --write <files>`. Spec anchor repointer is `node scripts/check-spec-anchor-names.mjs --fix <spec>` (NOT scripts/spec-links/reanchor.mjs, which does not exist here) — repoints #Lnn from the citation LABEL which must equal the it() title EXACTLY; my added helper lines shifted an existing citation L194->L211 and --fix repaired it. Run prettier BEFORE the anchor fix. eslint recommended config does NOT enable no-throw-literal / @typescript-eslint/only-throw-error, so `throw value` (unknown) in a test provider is lint-clean; test files gate on re-lint/require-spec-link (every it must be cited by a spec) + test-imports-its-subject + no-nondeterministic-tests. Did NOT run eslint/tsc/build (OOM risk per instructions; CI is judge).
</document>
</section>
</context>
